A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GT-SVJ and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. All content can be matched across layout changes. Appendices A and B are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Table 1, training and component ablations in Figures 4–6, and perturbation experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, training and component ablations, and Appendix A perturbation experiments.

M1.justification: Both retain the CogVideoX backbone, last-third LoRA adaptation, energy-based discrimination with five latent perturbations, and aspect-score regression followed by pairwise preference training. Appendix A's perturbation-sampling procedure is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same real/generated training-video coverage and VisionReward annotations, and evaluate GenAI-Bench, MonteBench, and VideoReward-Bench. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VideoScore, VisionReward, and VideoReward as comparators on all three benchmarks. Comparator membership in the main-text and appendix ablations is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The ties/no-ties evaluation, training corpus sizes, VisionReward splits, model sizes, and LoRA settings remain unchanged. Both specify 2–6-second truncations with probabilities 0.25 for discriminative training and 0.2 for preference training.

E4.justification: Both retain analyses of LoRA placement, discriminative initialization, perturbed negatives, and variable video lengths. Appendix A's individual-perturbation and combined-perturbation experiments are identical; relocated figures do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: The shaded training/validation plots and Appendix A.1's discussion of independent perturbation-training runs are unchanged. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated VideoReward-Bench deficit from roughly 7% to roughly 5%. Table 1 remains unchanged: without ties, VideoReward scores 73.59 and GT-SVJ 68.57, a 5.02-percentage-point or 6.82% relative gap. This revises the numerical summary, not measured performance. Other tabulated and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The energy-based and BT/BTT formulations, mathematical definitions of the five perturbations, and Appendix A's sampling and gradient-decay equations are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about generative-model reward learning, temporal discrimination, leading performance on GenAI-Bench and MonteBench, and reduced human-annotation requirements. Editorial rephrasing does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations involving harder negatives, discriminative features, temporal generalization, and the LoRA efficiency tradeoff. The VideoReward-Bench distribution-shift explanation and limitation concerning the absence of a conversational interface are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Hugging Face project URL to the abstract and identifies Delta, DeltaAI, Illinois Computes, and NAIRR computing support in a new acknowledgment. These expand access and resource documentation; the implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 42 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning against VLM-based evaluators and the ControlNeXt footnote. No cited work or scientific novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory paragraphs and the reward-model explanation, adjusts terminology capitalization and affiliations, adds an internship footnote, and introduces an acknowledgment section. These are localized editorial changes within the retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 5 to page 4, Figure 3 moves upward on page 5, and Figure 4's middle panel is vertically aligned with its neighbors. Text consequently reflows. Figure content, captions, table structures, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added project pointer and computing-resource disclosure modestly improve documentation, while tighter prose and figure alignment improve readability. Scientific evidence is unchanged. The benefit remains limited: Section 5.2's revised 5% wording leaves percentage-versus-percentage-point ambiguity, and the introduction still reports 7%.
